title: Positive tangent weights make every homogeneous Luna coordinate system global
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $Z$ be an affine $F$-scheme of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with a $\mathbf G_m$-action [def-sc-gm-ga], an $F$-morphism $\mathbf G_m\times_F Z\to Z$ satisfying the identity and associativity laws. Let $z\in Z(F)$ be fixed and put $A=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ and $\mathfrak m=\ker(A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_z}F)$. Write $\mathfrak m^2$ for the ideal generated by products of two elements of $\mathfrak m$. Assume $Z$ is smooth and connected [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Put $T_zZ=\operatorname{Hom}_F(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2,F)$ with the differentiated action. Assume it is a direct sum of character subspaces of strictly positive integer weights (an empty sum is allowed). Suppose $a_1,\ldots,a_d\in\mathfrak m$ have classes forming an $F$-basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ and satisfy $a_i(tu)=t^{n_i}a_i(u)$ for integers $n_i$. Let $\lambda:Z\to\mathbf A_F^d=\operatorname{Spec}F[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$ be the morphism induced by the $F$-algebra homomorphism $T_i\mapsto a_i$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then $\lambda$ is an isomorphism of $F$-schemes. There is no restriction on $\operatorname{char}F$, and when $d=0$ this asserts $Z\cong\operatorname{Spec}F$.

source.place: Theorem 13.41 and its proof, printed pp.269--270; the supplied homogeneous basis spans the invariant complement W defining a Luna map in Lemma 13.36 and the paragraph following Lemma 13.35.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to the structure morphism, with the affine opens $Z$ and $\operatorname{Spec}F$: $A$ is a finitely generated $F$-algebra. Thus [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] makes $A$ Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], $Z$ is regular. It is nonempty because it has the point $z$, and is connected by hypothesis, so [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] makes $Z$ integral. The definition [def-pc-integral-scheme], applied to the nonempty affine open $Z$ itself, says that $A$ is an integral domain. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](1) identifies $A_{\mathfrak m}$ with $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$; this is a regular local ring by regularity of $Z$.

source.place: Theorem 13.41, p.269, irreducible case; global smoothness here gives integrality immediately. Supporting Stacks Tags 01T2, 056S, 0569, 033N, 01OK, 01HV.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and the coordinate group law of [def-sc-gm-ga] to write the action on functions as an $F$-algebra map $c:A\to A[t,t^{-1}]$; by the clause of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] that every morphism of affine spectra is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of exactly one ring map, the identity and associativity laws and the fixedness of $z$, being equalities of morphisms of affine schemes, are equivalent to the corresponding identities of algebra maps used below. Its counit is evaluation at $t=1$ and its coassociativity uses $t\mapsto st$. For each $a$, write its unique finite Laurent expansion $c(a)=\sum_n a_nt^n$. Comparing the coefficient of $t^n$ in coassociativity gives $c(a_n)=a_ns^n$ (with $s$ the coaction variable), and the counit gives $a=\sum_n a_n$. If a finite sum of eigenvectors of distinct weights is zero, applying $c$ and comparing Laurent coefficients makes each summand zero. Hence $A=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}A_n$, where $A_n=\{a:c(a)=at^n\}$. Multiplicativity gives $1\in A_0$ and $A_rA_s\subseteq A_{r+s}$. Since $z$ is fixed, evaluation at $z$ sends $c(a)$ to the constant $a(z)$, so $a_n(z)=0$ for $n\ne0$ and $a_0(z)=a(z)$. In particular $\mathfrak m$ is homogeneous, and $A_n\subseteq\mathfrak m$ for $n\ne0$.

source.place: Theorem 13.41, p.269, first paragraph; explicit Laurent-coefficient argument from Theorem 12.12, pp.234--235. Affine product: Stacks Tags 01I4 and 01JQ.

proof.text: The supplied identity says $c(a_i)=a_it^{n_i}$, so $a_i$ is homogeneous for the grading of step 2. Let $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ be the basis of $\operatorname{Hom}_F(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2,F)$ dual to the classes of the $a_i$. For the differentiated point action $d\mu_t$, evaluation on these classes gives $(d\mu_t v_i)(\overline a_j)=v_i(\overline{a_j\circ\mu_t})=t^{n_j}\delta_{ij}$. Consequently $d\mu_t v_i=t^{n_i}v_i$. Each nonzero $v_i$ has strictly positive character weight by the tangent-weight hypothesis, so $n_i>0$ for every $i$. This calculation fixes the sign convention: these are the weights in $a_i(tu)=t^{n_i}a_i(u)$.

source.place: Lemma 13.35, pp.267--268, and Example 13.37, p.268: differential of the coordinate map and agreement of the coordinate and tangent weights.

proof.text: For every $j\ge1$, $\mathfrak m^j$ is homogeneous, since it is the additive span of products of $j$ elements of the homogeneous ideal $\mathfrak m$. The quotient $\mathfrak m^j/\mathfrak m^{j+1}$ is spanned over $F$ by the classes of the products $a_{i_1}\cdots a_{i_j}$. Indeed, write each of the $j$ factors of a generator of $\mathfrak m^j$ modulo $\mathfrak m^2$ as an $F$-linear combination of the $a_i$; every term in which one factor lies in $\mathfrak m^2$ belongs to $\mathfrak m^{j+1}$. Any coefficient from $A$ can be replaced by its residue in $A/\mathfrak m=F$, with the error again in $\mathfrak m^{j+1}$. These spanning products all have strictly positive weight by step 3, so this quotient has no homogeneous component of weight $\le0$. If $d=0$, all these quotients are zero by the same product calculation with an empty spanning set.

source.place: Theorem 13.41, p.269, displayed surjection from Sym^j(W) to m^j/m^{j+1}; explicit product calculation.

proof.text: Set $N=\bigcap_{j\ge0}\mathfrak m^j\subseteq A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-localization] with $R=A$, $I=\mathfrak m$, $M=A$, and the prime $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$. The ring is Noetherian by step 1; $A$ is generated by $1$ as an $A$-module, and $\mathfrak m$ is maximal since evaluation onto $F$ is surjective. The lemma gives $f\notin\mathfrak m$ such that every $x\in N$ is killed by some power $f^r$. Here $f\ne0$ because $0\in\mathfrak m$, and $A$ is a domain by step 1, so $f^rx=0$ implies $x=0$. Thus $\bigcap_j\mathfrak m^j=0$.

source.place: Tag 00IQ, lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module, part (1); Milne Theorem 13.41, p.269, Krull-intersection paragraph.

proof.text: Let $x\in\mathfrak m$ be homogeneous of weight $n\le0$. Starting with $x\in\mathfrak m$, induct on $j\ge1$. If $x\in\mathfrak m^j$, its class in $\mathfrak m^j/\mathfrak m^{j+1}$ has weight $n$, so step 4 makes that class zero and $x\in\mathfrak m^{j+1}$. Hence step 5 gives $x=0$. For $n<0$, step 2 puts $A_n$ in $\mathfrak m$, so $A_n=0$. For $x\in A_0$, the element $x-x(z)1$ belongs to $\mathfrak m\cap A_0$, hence is zero; thus $A_0=F\cdot1$, with $F\to A$ injective because evaluation splits it. Finally $\mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{n>0}A_n$: evaluation kills all positive components and has trivial kernel on $A_0$. Reindexing the remaining components gives the required $\mathbf N$-grading of $A$.

source.place: Theorem 13.41, p.269: deduce A_0=k, vanishing outside the positive monoid, and m equal to its positive part, using the separated filtration.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-positive-graded-regular-polynomial] with $B=A$ and $b_i=a_i$. Step 1 supplies finite generation over $F$ and regularity of $A_{\mathfrak m}$. Step 6 supplies the nonnegative grading with $A_0=F$ and positive-degree maximal ideal exactly $\mathfrak m$. The supplied classes are the required basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, and steps 2--3 show that their specified lifts are homogeneous of strictly positive degrees $n_i$. Therefore the actual evaluation homomorphism $\phi:F[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to A$, $T_i\mapsto a_i$, is an isomorphism of $F$-algebras. This conclusion applies to every supplied basis and lifts, rather than selecting a new coordinate map. The cited lemma includes the empty basis: when $d=0$, $\phi:F\to A$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Theorem 13.41, p.269, graded Nakayama and dimension argument, reused through the existing positive-graded regular-algebra lemma (Lemma 13.39 and Theorem 13.44).

proof.text: By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], applying $\operatorname{Spec}$ to $\phi$ and its inverse produces inverse $F$-scheme morphisms. In the affine identification $Z=\operatorname{Spec}A$, the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\phi$ is precisely the stipulated $\lambda$, since its coordinate map sends $T_i$ to $a_i$. Thus $\lambda$ is an isomorphism. If $d=0$, the same construction identifies $Z$ with $\operatorname{Spec}F$. No step used a restriction on the characteristic of $F$.

source.place: Theorem 13.41, p.269, passage from the symmetric-algebra map to the Luna map; polynomial basis identifies its target with affine d-space.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 13.41, pp.269--270, its irreducible-case proof; global smoothness and connectedness supply integrality using the cited regular-scheme input. The graded Nakayama/dimension conclusion is the existing lemma extracted from Lemma 13.39 and Theorem 13.44.
